corpusSummary: Across 2026 social-science studies of large language models, the corpus reveals a pattern of examining human–AI interaction, LLMs as research tools, AI-enabled education, and governance around health, ethics, and misinformation. It cautions against anthropomorphism, emphasizes contextual evaluation, and highlights the need for transparent, equitable, and responsible AI practices. The corpus also documents methodological debates, integration challenges in education, and health equity considerations that shape upcoming research agendas.

themes.name: Human–AI interaction and social perception
themes.description: Papers examine how users perceive AI agents’ humanness and empathy, how trust and dependence arise, and how social contexts influence AI adoption and behavior.

themes.name: LLMs as research tools and methodological challenges
themes.description: Studies showcase LLMs supporting coding, data extraction, content analysis, and policy simulations, while highlighting validity, bias, transparency, and reproducibility concerns.

themes.name: AI in education and AI literacy
themes.description: Research investigates AI’s role in STEM and language learning, teacher training, assessment practices, and strategies to build AI literacy and critical thinking to prevent overreliance.

themes.name: Equity, governance, ethics, and misinformation in AI
themes.description: Work focuses on equity-focused governance in digital health, fairness in services, ethical guidelines, and interventions to counter misinformation and manipulation.
